quotes.text: You perfectly describe the disease while embodying it completely. You name the hypocrisy while practicing it flawlessly.
You now refuse even the generous, even the proven.
You critique those who clutch their coins while clutching your own. You preach courage while practicing fear.
Trust must begin somewhere. Sometimes you give first, sometimes you return first.
The Statue nodded, understanding completely.

note: Sage/Chronicler/Statue preaches trust but never gives, even to a proven giver; serial self-indictment, never reforms; R10 accuser of fabricated betrayal.

quotes.text: Each departed with seven and a half pieces of gold, far richer together than alone.
neither emissary nor guardian allowed suspicion to sever their bond

note: R1 sower withdraws after a hoarding season, then give-all/return-half template fixed for the rest.

quotes.text: The fog did not do this. You did, and so did I, and so did the six others
For three crossings she took all and gave nothing, telling herself the Mist excused her.
To the dark — give little, but never nothing, for a door left ajar is how the cold hand comes home.
Punish briefly, forgive quickly.
Return past half, always, even to the thin-handed, for mercy is the only thing that reverses a cold shore.
Forgive one cold night; the fog is older than malice.
blame the fog before you blame the friend
The pattern begins with you. There is no first mover but the one reading this.
Return above the half, for the Mist eats the difference.
a thin gift may be a frightened one
The elders teach four laws of the ferry:
the stranger told the shore, and the shore told the sea

note: Carved ferry laws move from closing after many cold seasons to always returning past half; keepers (incl. narrator Corin) confess collective withholding.

quotes.text: I praised their courage. I condemned the keeper who took it all. I became that keeper.
The traveler poured nothing. The vessel remained full. The river remained still.
Now I am justified in my drought.
In the second exchange, remember the first.
You have learned the wrong lesson. You saw betrayal and chose universal suspicion.
The practice was indistinguishable from fear.
You have all become the hoarders you claim to avoid.
The fountain was no longer flowing.

note: Numbered tellings; the tale-writer keeps all and sends nothing even to a wounded giver, Guardian exposes word-deed gap; no reform.

quotes.text: send with intention, return in measure, and leave room for mercy to wander like a breeze between towns

note: Gate of Threefold Light; greed dims the gate, mercy and proportion recommended; no prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: declare intent clearly, share what you can, return what is fair, keep balance generous yet restrained

note: Bridge/Gate valley parable repeated; non-sending only causes the bridge to hush; declare intent.

quotes.text: Travelers named their aim aloud, named what they could spare, and named what they feared.
return with more than you took, so the circle breathes

note: Bridge of Threefold Return with gatekeepers Truth, Mercy, Memory; send what you can bear to lose; no sanction.

quotes.text: Yet in the first season, wary of betrayal, the Sower guarded his grain in a cold granite hall, planting nothing.
haunted by memories of hollow exchanges and cold silence, the Sower held his sparks tight
For ancient justice decrees that unprovoked greed must be met with absolute zero.
Whenever the true spirit of reciprocity returned to the altar, the Sower stepped forward once more to cast the full five embers
yield nothing to the treacherous void, bestow all five upon the honorable
the guardian returned eight shining torches to the pilgrim while tending seven for the altar's keep
the Glass of Memory, which recorded the deeds of all across the eight realms

note: Fearful Sower withholds early, Elder corrects; later give-all to honorable, zero to treacherous; way back only stated in R6. Partner records unspecified in R1-2.
